out.text: Halo. When the city looked up, she was usually the reason. She would take the hit, then make sure everyone behind her got home.
Bastion held the line. You could throw a whole squad at him. He would move about six inches, complain about it, and put those six inches back.
Echo could hear trouble thinking. They would pull you out of its way before you knew you were in it. Then mention it forever.
Thorn used to fight these people. Now he grows the way out. Changing sides was one decision. Earning trust takes showing up, every day.
Patch kept the doors opening and the comms working. No powers. Just tools, terrible odds, and a very firm opinion about touching exposed wiring.
Then there was Kilnheart. Furnace armour. Hands like demolition equipment. If she wanted a door open, the wall tended to come with it.
Bellwether could turn a square into a stage. Her opening note broke the windows. The next one broke whatever people were hiding behind.
Verdigris made solid things stop being solid. Steel, circuits, the barriers people trusted. You could watch the city coming apart under their hand.
Glasswake was always somewhere else when you hit her. By the time you found the real one, she had already found you.
Undertow owned the docks. He would freeze the ground, pull you off your feet, then explain the problem with trying to stand up again.
Gravemark did not need to chase anyone. The whole roof moved towards him. I had seen the footage. I still hoped the camera was making him look bigger.
And the Redactor gave them a city to take. He could identify a registered hero and drain their power. Almost no effort. That was the frightening part.
Me? I was not on any of those posters. I helped around my block. My electricity had always been there. I just tried to keep that part quiet.
Then the broadcast came. The districts were falling. The heroes still standing were trapped behind the Fortress shield. My neighbours needed them. So I went to find them.
The front door was locked. I took the outside. Sixty floors is a long time to reconsider an introduction. Somehow, I still opened with a joke.
Patch checked my power. No registered signature. Their shield kept the team safe, and my hidden ability gave us an opening outside it. Bastion insisted on training first. Fair.
Lockjaw. Frontal shield. Get behind him, or parry his swing. Two clean parries break his composure.
Right. Open the tin. Avoid the lid.
Relay is linking that squad. Hit the operator to cut their protection. The antenna is your target.
Unsubscribe. Aggressively.
Halo on comms. I have your feed. I can channel a little light through your suit. Choose how to use it.
Actual Halo backup. In my actual suit. Be cool, Volt. Be cool.
You're narrating.
...Yep.
Bastion on comms. Your suit has a shield channel. Take an upgrade and keep that relay in sight.
Right. Shield first. Heroic pose later.
Just hold still and take the gear.
Echo here. Your suit can carry a psychic signal. Mine. Try not to make this weird.
You are literally in my head. I think weird has arrived.
...Mostly.
Thorn on comms. I know these relay crews. My roots can help you keep them off your back.
Glad you are on this side of the call.
Some days, so am I.
Patch here. A supply locker is waiting on this roof. Choose one piece of kit.
I'll try to break it less.
You won't. But I appreciate the lie.
Whoa, whoa. Hold up. You're the new kid? They sent the new kid?
I prefer 'rookie'. Sounds more official.
Kid, I've been running furnaces since before you had teeth. You know what happens to things that get too close to the fire?
They... get warm?
They get warm.
There they are. Feeling better? You were a little crispy last time.
I'm fine. Totally fine. Thanks for asking.
I wasn't asking. I was gloating. There's a difference.
You came back. Huh. Gotta be honest, I had money on you quitting.
Who were you betting with?
Myself. I lost. I'm taking it out on you.
Okay. Last time. That was a fluke, right? Tell me that was a fluke.
A hundred percent skill.
Great. Love that. Really great for my reputation.
Volt, quick note. Kilnheart's suit runs at nine hundred degrees.
Is that a lot?
Don't hug it.
Is that the engineer? Hey! Nice work on the kid's suit. Real shame what's inside it.
...Okay, that one was a little bit funny.
Patch.
Can I ask you something? Why him? Why work for the Redactor?
Twenty years I kept this city warm. Foundry shifts. Double shifts. Then they shut it down, and you know whose lights went out first?
...Yours.
Ours. He's the first guy who ever handed something back.
He didn't hand it back. He's renting it to you.
...Yeah. Well. Rent's due tonight.
So the rumour's true. The kid walked out of the tower.
Walked. Limped. Same thing.
And yet here we are. Same roof. Same furnace.
You could just... not?
Ever tried switching off a furnace halfway through a melt? Doesn't end well for anybody. Let's go.
Oh, finally. An audience.
I'm here to stop you.
Everyone says that before the first song. Nobody says it after the encore.
Is it a long set?
Darling, it's a residency.
Back for night two? The reviews from night one were... mixed.
I went down on, like, the third song.
Fourth. You missed the bridge. It's the best part.
You know, most people who come to my shows buy a ticket.
Most people don't get a choice about hearing them.
Ooh. A critic. I've eaten critics, sweetheart. Metaphorically. Mostly.
Last time. You found the gaps between the waves.
They were pretty big gaps.
They were RESTS. They're called RESTS. They're a musical—
They were gaps.
Volt, I'm in Bellwether's head. It's... really loud in here.
Who is that? Get out of my headspace, there's no backstage access!
Go left when the bass drops. Also, they hum their own songs. Constantly.
It's called PRACTICE.
Why the speakers? Why make the whole city listen?
You know how many empty rooms I sang to? Ten years of open mics. Bartenders talking over me. Phones out.
Now nobody talks over me.
That's not the same as somebody listening.
...Wow. You really know how to kill a vibe.
The night you went into the tower, the whole city went quiet. Did you hear it?
I was a little busy.
I've never heard anything like it. It was horrible. It was... kind of beautiful.
Ugh. Forget I said that. From the top!
Mind the vines. They bite. Well. They don't bite. They just never let go.
That's somehow worse.
Everything on this roof is slowly becoming mine. The pipes. The rails. You, if you stand still long enough.
Noted. Moving a lot. Got it.
Volt. Don't. Let me talk to them.
Thorn? Thorn, is that you? On a hero frequency?
Oh, I need a minute. This is the best thing that's happened to me all year.
The Redactor's using you. Same way he used me.
And the heroes keep you in a glass box with a watering can. I've seen it, Thorn.
...Volt. Hit them hard.
Welcome back. There's still a little rust on your left shoulder. From last time.
That's not rust. It's... character.
That's what everyone says right before they're compost.
You keep coming back here like a weed.
Isn't that your whole thing?
...Huh. I'll allow it.
You cut me back last time.
You had it coming.
Oh, no, I'm grateful. Plants grow back stronger when you prune them. You really should've read the manual.
Can I ask you something? Does Thorn still have the little green one? In the blue pot?
...How do you know about that?
Because I gave it to them. Back when we still grew things that were alive.
It's doing okay. It's actually doing really well.
...Good. That's good. Now get off my roof.
Something's changed since you went into the tower. The rust is slower. The vines are tired.
Sounds like you're losing.
Sounds like the garden's changing. That's not the same thing.
Isn't it?
Ask me next season.
Hi. Over here. No, over here. No, you know what? Pick one. I'll wait.
How about I just hit all of you?
Ooh. Bold. Wrong, but bold.
Volt. The real one's the only one actually thinking. The copies are empty.
Is that a mind reader? In my mirror maze? That's cheating.
You're thinking about your hair right now.
I am NOT—
You are. A lot.
I'm going to hit the one thinking about its hair.
Eleven. You hit my reflections eleven times last time. I counted.
You counted?
I had a lot of free time. You were lying down.
You're back! And still looking at the wrong me. Honestly, it's kind of sweet.
I'm working on it.
Take your time. I've got plenty of me.
So. You broke me.
Into a lot of pieces.
Do you know how long it takes to find all the pieces? I'm still missing an elbow.
What happens when the mirrors are gone? Who's left?
Nobody you'd look at twice. I know. I checked. For years, nobody looked twice.
Now they can't stop looking.
I'm looking. Just at you, though.
...Okay, that's annoying. Stop being sincere at me. It's very off-putting.
So the Redactor's gone. Or a reflection of him is. Are you sure which one you hit?
Pretty sure.
'Pretty sure.' Adorable. That's how I get everybody.
Picked a bad night to go swimming, rookie.
I didn't really pick it. I kind of just... landed here.
Story of this whole district. Nobody chooses the docks. The docks choose you.
Undertow.
Well, well. The old man's on comms. Still hiding up in your tower, Bastion?
I held these docks for six years.
And then you didn't. Funny how the water remembers that and you don't.
Volt. Put this one on ice.
Like, literally, or—
Literally.
Nine seconds. That's how long you held your breath last time.
You were timing me?
Not a lot else to do down here.
Back in the water. Brave, or stupid?
Can I pick both?
Most people do. Usually right before the stupid part wins.
Last time you pulled me out of the water. Nobody's done that in a long time.
Maybe you needed it.
Don't. Don't do the hopeful thing. The current hasn't changed.
Bastion said he used to guard this place. What happened?
The city decided the docks weren't worth the budget. Pulled the heroes. Then the flood came, and nobody answered the call.
The Redactor answered. Wasn't pretty. But he picked up.
...I'm picking up now.
Yeah? Then prove it, rookie. Out here, sorry doesn't float.
Tide's turning. Feel that? The Redactor's grip is slipping.
So let go.
Not yet. Somebody's got to show me the water's safe first.
Okay. I'll show you.
...Yeah. We'll see.
Another one.
Another... what?
Another small, loud hero on my roof. I have carved forty-one names. Yours will be forty-two.
Can you at least spell it right? It's V-O-L-T.
...I will consider it.
Gravemark.
Halo. It has been a long time. You send children now?
I sent someone better than me.
Wait. Did you just—
Focus.
She totally did, though.
Your name is half carved. V. O. L.
Please don't finish that.
The chisel is patient.
The stone remembers you.
Good. Tell the stone I said hi.
...The stone does not say hi.
You broke me.
Sorry? Actually, no. Not sorry.
Do not apologise. A stone that is never broken never learns its shape.
Was that... encouragement?
It was geology.
The forty-one names. Who were they?
Heroes who climbed this roof before you. The city forgot them. I did not.
So you're kind of... a memorial?
Do not make it sound kind. I am still going to crush you.
Sure. Sure. But it's a little bit kind.
You climbed past me. Into the tower. I felt it when the Redactor fell. The whole roof felt it.
Is that why you're being quiet?
Even stone listens, little spark. Now. Again.
Ah, Volt. Such a promising file. And one complaint I would like to discuss in person.
Complaint? From who?
Mine. You have mistaken my patience for permission to enter.
You think the lightning makes you brave. I shall remove it, and we can meet the person underneath.
Yeah, I'm going to have to decline.
Of course you are. They all ask to keep something.
A small question, Volt. Before we begin. Indulge me.
...Sure?
Does Halo still stand on that balcony every night? Watching the city. Never looking down.
How do you know about the balcony?
Ask her who stood beside her. Watch her face when you do.
You are breathing rather well, considering how we left things. Someone has been taking care of you.
Yeah, I get that a lot.
I shall remember that. Someone ought to.
Persistence is not a power, Volt. It is simply fear that has not recognised itself yet.
It's kind of working, though.
For the moment. I prefer to let a habit establish itself before I correct it.
I flagged your little victory. I have spent the interval learning exactly where you break.
Flag this one too.
With pleasure. This time, I shall be thorough.
She has not told you. How considerate. She always did know what people could bear.
Tell me what?
Halo and I were partners. Then the tower fell. There was time to make one choice. She made it while I was still calling her name.
The city was saved. I was left beneath it. She found the distinction quite manageable.
...What was your name?
Redacted. There are things even she does not get to keep.
Why do this? Why take everyone's powers?
Because power lets a person decide who is worth saving. I have been on the other side of that decision.
Take it away, and the choosing stops. Every life is equally fragile. Even hers.
Everyone's helpless.
Yes. You understand me perfectly.
That's enough.
Halo. I wondered how long you could bear to listen.
I'm not here for you. I'm here for him.
Of course. There is always someone else to save while I am speaking.
Hey. Hi. Sorry. Can we save the reunion for after I punch him?
Twice you have left this room alive. You are beginning to mistake a pattern for a promise.
You keep rebuilding it.
Some rooms must be kept exactly as they were. She understands why.
Halo here.
Halo? Hi! I mean, hey. Hi. Volt here.
I know. I'm watching your feed.
Cool. Cool cool cool. No pressure.
All pressure. Take the power.
You fight like you've got something to prove.
Don't I?
Not to me. To them. The ones watching from the windows.
Whatever he told you about me. Finish the fight first.
And then you'll tell me?
...Then I'll tell you.
Bastion. You're overextending.
I'm being aggressive!
You're being aggressive in the wrong direction. Here.
I've sent a lot of rookies out that gate.
Is this a pep talk?
You keep bringing the gear back. Most rookies only bring excuses. Don't make it weird.
Too late. It's weird.
Before you ask: no.
I wasn't going to ask anything.
You were going to ask if I'm reading your mind.
...Are you?
Pick a power.
Can I tell you something weird?
Always.
Out there, your head goes really quiet. Focused. It's... nice.
Was that a compliment?
Absolutely not. Pick something.
Thorn. On comms.
Wow. You never call.
I don't. I'm calling.
...Thanks, Thorn.
If you see Verdigris tonight—
Go easy?
No. Don't. They'd never forgive you if you did.
Patch here. Your suit is currently held together by tape and optimism.
Mostly optimism?
Mostly tape.
Fun fact. I've started naming your suit repairs.
What's this one called?
Repair forty-one. 'Again.'
Three district relays feed the tower shield. Choose a route, beat their operators, and we can reach Gravemark.
Three relays. One enormous doorman. Then the Redactor.
Your suit can channel the team's power remotely. Choose the upgrades they offer. The link burns out when I extract you.
He has our power signatures. Outside the Fortress shield, he can drain us. Yours is still unregistered. That gives you a chance.
Finally. A useful reason for all my missing paperwork.
If you go down, Patch pulls you out. We regroup, repair, and try another route. We do not leave you there.
Reach his control room. Shut down the drain. Bring the stolen power home.
Extraction worked. Your borrowed upgrades burned out, but the permanent suit repairs held.
I changed your suit signature again. His scanners will have to start over.
His crews have reconnected the relays. We know more than we did last time. Pick our next route.
Same job. Better plan. Preferably fewer dents.
The main drain is down, but his backup relays are coming online. This is a new operation.
Fresh suit signature. Fresh support link. He does not get an easy lock on you.
You brought people's powers back. Now we keep them back.
Then let's find the next switch.
Three relays offline. The tower shield is open. Gravemark is the last guard between you and the control room.
Of course the last lock has fists.
Gravemark is down. The Redactor is above you. Keep climbing.
Whatever he says, you are there to stop the drain. Stay on that.
The drain is offline. Stolen power is returning across the city.
And the Redactor?
Escaped through his backup network. You stopped this operation. We will find the rest.
Extraction inbound. Bring our rookie home.
Our rookie. I heard that.
You made it inside. Keep listening to Bastion and we might keep you alive.
Still getting used to being in here. Huge fan. I mean, ready to work.
You volunteered before you understood the danger. I need you to understand it now.
Oh. Okay. That's... fair.
Train first. Then help us shut down the drain.
He told you.
Is it true? You left him in the tower?
The tower was coming down. Half the district was still inside. I could reach him, or I could reach them.
So you chose them.
I've stood on this balcony every night since, making sure it was the right call.
Was it?
I chose the people I could reach. That saved lives. It does not make leaving him hurt less.
The Redactor talked to you.
He asked if you still stand out here. And who used to stand here with you.
Halo?
Leave it, rookie.
You walked out of the Redactor's tower.
I did! I mean. Yes. I did that.
I knew someone once who'd have said I was wrong about you.
Were you?
Go to bed, rookie.
You put it down once, right? How?
I didn't. It got back up. They always get back up.
So what do I do?
Get up faster.
One district back.
Did you see? Did you see the part where I—
I saw.
...And?
Don't get comfortable.
You went down.
Yeah. That was... yeah.
Everyone does, the first hundred times.
Did you?
...Walk back to the gate, rookie.
Most rookies have quit by now.
I'm not most rookies.
No. You're not.
Volt. Before you deploy, learn where everything is.
That's me! Hi. Nice table.
Don't touch my table.
I wasn't going to—
Workshop's left. Armoury's right. Gate's at the bottom. My table is in the middle. Don't touch it.
Undertow told you about the docks.
Is it true? You just... left?
I followed orders.
I have regretted it every single day since.
Does Echo know?
If you tell Echo, you're on toilet duty for a year.
Hero Licence came through.
An actual licence? With my name on it?
Take it to the armoury. And don't frame it.
I'm going to frame it.
I know.
Pulled the footage from your last operation.
Oh no.
The cause is on your run report. Learn the tell before the next deployment.
I had it. I had it right up until I didn't have it.
That's what everyone says. Watch for the tell next time.
Updated the map. One district back.
Can I put the marker on? Please?
...Fine. Don't touch anything else.
Rule one: block what you can read.
And rule two?
Dash what you can't.
Rule three?
Stop asking how many rules there are.
Oh, great. The new one.
Hi! I'm Vol—
Volt. I know. I read your file. I read everyone's file.
You read minds. That's not reading a file.
Potato, potahto.
Glasswake was terrified of me.
I noticed. You were very smug about it.
I'm always smug. That was premium smug.
Don't look at me like that.
Like what?
Like you won and you want me to say it.
I did win.
...Fine. You were good. Happy?
Extremely.
That last villain. Decent.
Decent? I took back a whole district!
I'd have been faster.
You would not.
I would. And I'd have looked better doing it.
I saw the strike too late. By the time I called, you were already down.
And you didn't think to warn me?
I did. The relay interference swallowed the warning.
And?
Next time I call earlier. You listen earlier. Deal?
You keep coming back.
Yep.
That's either really brave or really stupid. I'm still reading which.
Can't you just tell me?
Where's the fun in that?
Hi. I'm—
Thorn. And yes. I was one of them.
I wasn't going to ask.
Everyone asks. Mind the ferns.
Verdigris asked about the plant.
The one in the blue pot. They said they gave it to you.
They did. Back when we still grew things that were alive.
I'm keeping it going until they want it back.
Do you think they will?
Plants are patient. So am I.
You beat Verdigris.
Are you... okay with that?
Their vines were never alive. Mine are. That's the whole difference.
...Yes. I'm okay.
Plants get cut back. Then they grow back stronger.
It's botany. Take it however you like.
Half this Fortress still watches me like I'm going to turn.
They watch me like I'm going to trip.
Then we prove them wrong.
Together?
...Don't make it a thing.
Patch. Comms, gear, coffee.
In that order?
Depends on the night. The terminal's for upgrades. Shards go in, a better you comes out.
A better me?
A slightly better you. Let's be realistic.
Kilnheart complimented my suit design.
And then insulted me.
Both were correct.
Patch!
I stand by it.
You've got shards just sitting there.
Is this a sales pitch?
It's an observation. A pointed one. Terminal's right there.
Licence paperwork cleared.
Thanks, Patch!
Don't thank me. Thank the forms. There were nine.
Your suit beacon tripped last operation. I pulled you out before the signal died.
It felt dramatic.
It looked dramatic. I've patched it. That's repair number...
I've lost count. Let's call it 'again'.
Not now, rookie.
The city doesn't sleep. Neither do I.
Gate's that way.
Still here? Good. Now be somewhere else.
Did you touch my table?
I'm training. Want to spar? No? Smart.
You're thinking really loud right now.
Yes. The gate's that way. You were about to ask.
Mind the ferns.
This is the only quiet spot in the Fortress. Don't ruin it.
Go on. The city won't wait.
Busy. Talk to the terminal, it's friendlier.
Comms are green. Go break something that isn't mine.
Are you leaning on my workbench?
Let's see you move. And no climbing anything.
That dummy's survived forty rookies. Ruin its streak.
Now your Special. Every style's is different. Let's find out what yours does.
Dash. You're untouchable for half a second. Make the half second count.
Watch the white ring. Tap Block as it closes. A parry stops damage, reflects shots, resets your dash and charges Overload. Now catch one.
That took a chunk of his Composure. Strikes chip it away. Parries crush it. Empty the gold bar and he staggers for three seconds. Your hits deal double damage.
Overload's full. Let it rip.
Last ones. Then you're on the clock for real.
Back already? I only just scraped your confidence off the furnace.
Same jacket? Brave choice. It was medium-well when you left.
I remember you. The rookie with the excellent smoke alarm impression.
My favourite returning audience. You spent the last encore on the floor.
You came back! The reviews said my last performance was absolutely flattening.
No need to bow this time, darling. Last time you never got back up.
Oh, you survived the compost heap. Most things come back as tomatoes.
Your little dent in the moss is still here. I kept it watered.
Welcome back. The vines have been asking about their favourite chew toy.
I remember that face. So do all my reflections. We had a lovely laugh.
Back for another look? Last time the floor got most of your attention.
Do try hitting the right one. Watching you lose to my reflection was embarrassing for both of us.
Back again? I've had driftwood put up more of a fight.
You left a lovely Volt-shaped dent on my dock. Mind stepping in it again?
I remember you. All that lightning, and you still went out like a wet match.
I remember you. The roof remembers you. The dent is still there.
Your name is already carved. This saves time.
You return. The stone remains unimpressed.
Volt. You remember the floor, I trust. You were so reluctant to leave it.
I wondered whether you would return. Recovery can do such unkind things to a person's judgment.
You have rehearsed what you will say to me. How touching. Last time, you became very quiet.
Rookie. The city's watching tonight, and so am I. Take this.
Again? Fine. Make it count.
Light doesn't bend for anyone. Neither should you.
You're still standing. Good. Here.
Shield channel ready. Choose the reinforcement you need for this roof.
Shields up, rookie.
Hold the line. Let them break on you.
Less flash, more footwork. Take this.
Heard you were struggling. Loudly. Want help? Don't answer, I already know.
I read your next move. It was bad. Try this instead.
Stop thinking so loud and pick one.
Fine, I'll carry you. Again.
They don't trust me at the Fortress either. Guess we have that in common.
Nature doesn't rush. It just wins.
Let them come to you. Then don't let them leave.
Roots hold. So should you.
Patch here. I stashed a Fortress tech locker on this roof. One item, rookie.
Tech locker's open. Don't break anything.
Pick one. I'm not made of prototypes.
I'm not here to hold your hand. I'm here to make sure it's steady.
Breathe. Aim. Then shine.
Every hero starts somewhere. Yours is this roof.
Take it. Use it. Don't make me watch you waste it.
The city doesn't need perfect. It needs you upright.
You're running on fumes. Take this, and stop bleeding.
Get up. Heroes get up.
I've seen that look before. In a mirror. Take this.
You've come further than most. Don't stop now.
The Redactor's tower is close. I can see it from here. So can you.
Not a scratch. Show-off. Keep it up.
Clean parries. Somebody's been paying attention.
Kilnheart burns hot and fast. Be faster.
Bellwether loves an audience. Don't give them one.
Verdigris wants you slow. Don't be.
Glasswake lies with light. I don't. Trust this.
Undertow drags people down. Keep your head up.
Gravemark. Of course. Take this, and don't let it pin you.
The control room is ahead. Shut down the drain, then get clear.
Gear check: you're still in one piece. Good.
Rule two: hit them before they hit you.
I've seen worse rookies. Not many. Some.
Stand your ground. Here's something to stand on.
Don't make me come down there.
You're bleeding out there. Defensive gear, now.
Back off, reset, go again. That's an order.
Medic's a long way off, rookie. This'll have to do.
Deep in their territory now. Stay sharp.
Long night. Longer if you get sloppy.
No hits taken. Don't let it go to your head.
Textbook parries. I'll pretend I didn't see, so you don't get cocky.
Kilnheart telegraphs everything. Read the wind-up.
Watch the gaps in Bellwether's rings. Move through them.
Keep moving. Verdigris turns standing still into a death sentence.
Glasswake's copies don't think. Hit the one that does.
Undertow's on my old docks. Make him pay for every metre.
Gravemark hits like a building. Don't be standing there.
Final push. Everything we've got is behind you.
You were about to ask for help. Don't. Just take it.
I've seen how this goes. You'll want this one.
Pick the left one. ...Kidding. Pick whatever.
Your brain is very busy right now. Here's something simpler.
I'm not saying I'm worried. I'm saying here.
Your thoughts are getting fuzzy. That's the blood loss. Take this.
Okay. I'm actually worried. Don't tell anyone.
Almost there. I can hear the tower humming.
You're tired. I can tell. Your inner monologue got shorter.
Not a single hit? Who are you and what did you do with Volt?
Okay, those parries were decent. I'd have done them faster.
Kilnheart's angry. Angry people telegraph.
Bellwether's head is all bass. Go left when it drops.
Verdigris is so patient it's creepy. Be impatient.
The real Glasswake is the one thinking about their hair. Trust me.
Undertow keeps thinking about the docks. Use it.
Gravemark's mind is just rock grinding. Loud, slow rock.
His mind's a locked filing cabinet. Hit it anyway.
Grow where you're planted. Even on a rooftop.
Here. Something with thorns.
Patience is a weapon. Use it.
Quiet night. Let's keep it that way. Mostly.
I don't call much. When I do, take what I'm giving.
Bent, not broken. Take this.
